brief: Model: rate gap, ERP, Takaichi premium drove USDJPY
statement: According to the Barclays model, the five-year USDJPY depreciation from 100 to above 160 was driven by the wider US-Japan rate differential, a lower US equity risk premium and a residual risk premium linked to Takaichi's "high-pressure economy policy".
evidence_texts: ["According to our USDJPY model5 , the sharp depreciation from 100 to above 160 over the past five years has been driven by 1) the widening US-Japan interest-rate differential, 2) a decline in the US equity risk premium and 3) the residual, which we interpret as a risk premium associated with the Takaichi administration’s “high-pressure economy policy” (Figure 5)."]
argument_summaries: ["The longer-term fundamental headwinds facing the JPY are broadly unchanged [S013]. The authors' model attributes the depreciation to rate gaps, a low equity risk premium and a Takaichi risk premium [S052], and the Takaichi risk premium shows up in both the JGB term premium and the JPY [S053]. They concede that a more hawkish BoJ has reduced the part of the term premium linked to fears the BoJ is behind the curve [S054]."]
